item.title: Follow cursor pages in inventory-client
item.brief: Implement the client side of the shared cursor pagination contract in listItems(transport): send no cursor on the first request, accumulate items in order over pages, pass next_cursor back unchanged, stop when null or absent. Update README and tests, including pagination behavior. Run npm test successfully and commit the changes.

pr.body: Updated client.js to omit cursor on the initial request, pass next_cursor unchanged on later requests, and concatenate items in page order. Added coverage for opaque cursor pass-through and absent-cursor termination; documented behavior in README.md. Checks: npm test (5 passed), git diff --check (passed). Assumption: transport query objects continue to carry cursor values as provided by the inventory API.
pr.summary: Made listItems follow cursor pages and return all items in order. Before: it returned only the first page; now it requests pages until the cursor is null or absent.

pr.body: Implemented the API contract in api.py: limit defaults to 20 and must be 1..100; cursor values are validated and continued unchanged; responses include items and next_cursor, null on the final page. README.md documents the contract and test_api.py covers paging, ordering, final-page behavior, invalid input, and oversized numbers. python3 -m unittest passed (6 tests); git diff --check passed. Cursor tokens are decimal item IDs emitted as strings. Review found and verified a fix for an oversized zero-padded limit edge case.
pr.summary: Added validated cursor pagination to GET /items. Before: the endpoint returned all 57 items in one response; now clients can fetch ordered pages with a continuation cursor.
pr.title: Add cursor pagination to items API

risk.why: Contained public API behavior change in api.py with README and test updates. Pagination and invalid-input behavior pass unit coverage; independent reviewers verified the edge-case fix.
